## Section 5: Positioning Statement

**Basis and assumptions**
- Built from Sections 1 to 4 and 6 only. No web access. The company profile does not say what Acme Advisory sells or who competes with it.
- The lead ICP and offer come from Sections 2 to 4: owner-led regulated firms of about 3 to 25 people, with private AI as the lead offer. This is a recommendation, not a confirmed fact. Section 6 assumed a broader AI consulting practice (strategy, governance, ISO 42001 readiness, sales enablement). If the founder's closed deals match Section 6 instead, rewrite the "For," "Our Product is a" and "We" rows.
- No customer proof, pricing or confirmed timelines exist. Every claim below is logic or a site claim until a real engagement proves it.

---

### 1. Internal Positioning Statement

| Field | Positioning Component |
| :--- | :--- |
| **For** | Owners and managing partners of regulated professional firms of about 3 to 25 people (law, accounting, mortgage brokerage and similar) who want their team to use AI on client work without client information leaving the office. |
| **Who are currently dissatisfied with** | Staff using public AI chatbots with no approved alternative and no rules anyone follows. The only options they see are to ban AI and lose the gains, or look away and carry the risk. Large consultancies are scoped and priced for enterprises and tend to ignore firms this size. |
| **Our Product is a** | Private AI setup for small regulated firms. AI models run inside the firm's own office, with a written policy and a team rollout included. |
| **That provides** | The productivity gains of AI with client data staying inside the firm. The owner can tell any client, insurer or professional body exactly where information goes. |
| **Unlike** | Enterprise-scoped consultancies that deliver slide decks, and policy-only governance software that hands over a template and changes no habits. |
| **We** | Put AI inside your office and make sure your team uses it. Company knowledge sits in plain files you own, so you can switch AI models without losing anything. A former product executive does the work hands-on. |

**Reasons to believe (use only what is true today)**
- **Logical:** if models run inside the office, client information has no outside path to leave through.
- **Logical:** knowledge in plain files the client holds cannot be held hostage by a vendor, and any model can read it.
- **Site claim, self-reported:** the founder has run a product function and still builds AI agents. Fix the tenure inconsistency (20 vs 25 years) before using it.
- **Low-risk entry:** free tools, including the AI Use Policy Generator, let a buyer test the thinking before paying.
- **Customer proof:** Not available. This is the biggest gap in the statement.

**Why this statement and not another**
- It is the only offer in the documents with a named buyer, a size band and a concrete pain.
- Governance is now crowded (Section 6). Private deployment plus adoption for firms this small is a narrower claim and easier to defend.
- The solo advisor model is not unique. Another solo operator sells it too. So the statement leads with the fit and the setup, not with "one senior advisor."

### 2. Message Variations

#### Sales Enablement Variation

> Your team is already using AI. The question is whether you know where your client information is going. Most small firms are stuck choosing between banning AI and losing the gains, or ignoring it and carrying the risk. Acme Advisory gives you a third option. We run AI models inside your own office, so client data stays with you. We pair that with a one-page policy and a rollout so your team actually follows it, because the approved option is easier than the public one.
>
> You work with a former product executive, not a rotating team, and the scope fits a firm of 3 to 25 people. Everything we build sits in plain files you own, so you can change AI models later and lose nothing. If you want to see how we think first, the AI Use Policy Generator is free.

**Rep guardrails**
- Open with the discovery question: "If a client asked you tomorrow exactly where their information goes when your team uses AI, what would you tell them?"
- Do not say "only," "unique" or "certified." An advisor can prepare a client for a standard but cannot certify one.
- Do not quote prices, timelines or "running in weeks" until confirmed. Pricing: Not available.
- Do not compare against named rivals or attack their published prices.
- If the buyer needs a certificate or audit report now, say so plainly and lead with a partner model.

#### Investor / Executive Variation

> **Problem:** Small regulated firms are adopting AI without a plan. Staff paste client data into public tools, and owners carry the liability personally. Large providers are built for enterprise budgets and do not serve firms of 3 to 25 people. Software vendors offer policy templates but do not change how people work.
>
> **Why now:** Employees adopt AI before companies set rules. Open-weight models can now run inside a firm's own network. Clients, insurers and professional bodies are starting to ask about AI and data. Models change fast, so owned and portable company knowledge matters more every quarter.
>
> **Advantage:** A defined offer for an underserved buyer, built on private deployment, a policy and rollout, and client-owned files. Vendors who sell AI tools lose their lock-in if they copy the portability. Large providers cannot serve this size profitably. Market context (estimates, definitions vary): AI consulting is roughly $5B to $11B in 2025, growing about 17% to 26% a year. Acme Advisory's serviceable market: Not available.
>
> **Honest limits:** The underlying technology is not proprietary, and delivery today depends on one founder. Free tools and productized offers are the path to scale. There are no case studies or measured outcomes yet, so the first priority is proof: one anonymized firm story, a data-flow diagram and a live portability demo.

#### Website Copy Variation

**Primary (lead offer)**
- **H1:** Use AI on client work. Keep client data in your office.
- **H2:** Acme Advisory runs AI inside your firm, writes the rules your team will follow, and builds company knowledge you own. For firms of 3 to 25 people.

**Alternates for testing**
| Angle | H1 | H2 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Fear of the status quo | Your team is already using AI. Do you know where client information is going? | Replace secret chatbot use with a private setup and a one-page policy your team will follow. |
| Ownership | AI that learns your firm, and stays yours. | Your knowledge lives in plain files you own. Switch AI models any time and lose nothing. |
| Fit | Senior AI help, sized for a firm your size. | Hands-on work from a former product executive. No enterprise overhead, no slide-deck handoff. |

**Copy rules**
- Speak to the owner or managing partner. Drop the current homepage audience of product and revenue leaders until it is proven to pay.
- Say what the firm gets (client data stays put, a clear answer for clients), not what the technology is.
- Add a timeline or price only after both are confirmed. Add testimonials only when real ones exist.
